name: _sparse_broadcast_to
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::_sparse_broadcast_to(Tensor(a) self, int[] size) -> Tensor(a). This representative overload is not exclusive; the original Gems pytest (tests/test__sparse_broadcast_to.py and benchmark/test__sparse_broadcast_to.py) owns the full contract for overloads, argument and keyword forms, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and must never be narrowed, have workloads deleted, or have reference semantics adapted to fit this one signature. All registered schemas supplied for this operator, verbatim: default: aten::_sparse_broadcast_to(Tensor(a) self, int[] size) -> Tensor(a). Semantics derived from the tests: the operator broadcasts a sparse COO operand to target `size`. New leading extents become new sparse dims and replicate the stored entries prod(new leading extents) times for the non-zero leading extents the pytest generates; a target whose leading extent is 0 is excluded by the pytest as an unresolved native hazard, so no rule for it is established here. An existing size-1 sparse dim may expand and likewise replicates entries; size-1 dense (payload) dims widen the payload only, leaving nnz unchanged; every other dim must equal the corresponding source dim. The COO result therefore keeps dense_dim(), reports sparse_dim() == len(size) - dense_dim(), and stores nnz * prod(new leading extents) * prod(expanded sparse singleton extents) entries, copied rather than recomputed (the pytest compares the raw COO result exactly, with zero tolerance). The result tensor carries the same alias set `a` as `self` in the schema, so the native implementation may hand back a tensor sharing storage with the input (an identity-size broadcast of a coalesced operand stays coalesced); the pytest does not assert output/input aliasing and instead snapshots the operand to prove it is not mutated. Rejection behavior remains in pytest: size values the schema cannot accept (None, non-sequence, non-integer or nested extents, empty size, rank drop, shorter-than-source, or a non-singleton dim that neither matches nor is 1) raise TypeError or RuntimeError, and a missing `size` raises TypeError or RuntimeError. Dense or CSR operands raise NotImplementedError, but those layout cases are collected only when the vendor string is nvidia; on other backends no layout-rejection case runs, and the two rejections were observed on the CUDA backend only. Backward is intentionally uncovered because the native operator exposes no autograd formula.
